redaction.segregability.summary: If a record contains both disclosable and non-disclosable information and the disclosable portion is intelligible, the entity must allow access to the disclosable information and may deny the exempt information by issuing a notice of denial.

classification.record_classification_sch.summary: An entity is not required to classify a particular record, record series, or information until access to the record is requested.

production.format_and_medium.summary: An entity must provide an electronic copy in lieu of paper if the requester prefers electronic, the entity currently maintains a reproducible electronic format providable without reformatting/conversion, and the copy does not disclose exempt records or can be segregated without undue expenditure.

production.certified_copy.summary: An entity must provide a certified copy of a record if the person has a right to inspect it, identifies it with reasonable specificity, and pays the lawful fees.

production.inspection_access.summary: An entity may not use the physical form (electronic or otherwise) in which a record is stored to deny or unreasonably hinder inspection or copying.

For a request of more than 50 pages, an entity may allow the requester to make the copies (using entity facilities or the requester's own) where the files contain no exempt records or can be segregated and reasonable safeguards are provided.

production.no_duty_to_create_or_convert.summary: In responding, an entity is not required to create a record; compile/format/manipulate/package/summarize/tailor information; or provide a record in a format, medium, or program not currently maintained.

eligibility.incarcerated_requester_exclu.summary: An entity is not required to respond to a request by or on behalf of an individual on parole or confined in a correctional facility, except for the first five requests per calendar year seeking only records referencing that individual, or a request submitted by the individual's attorney.

eligibility.any_person.summary: Any person has the right to inspect a public record free of charge and to take a copy during normal working hours, subject to the fee and response sections.

eligibility.no_purpose_requirement.summary: A requester need not state a reason or purpose; purpose is not among the required contents of a records request.

eligibility.no_residency_requirement.summary: The right of access runs to 'a person' with no residency or citizenship qualification imposed by GRAMA.

Master.s1.label: Fee-waiver requested

fee.waiver.summary: An entity may (and is encouraged to) fulfill a request without charge if release primarily benefits the public, the requester is the subject of/specified in the record, or the requester's legal rights are directly implicated and the requester is impecunious.

Master.s2.city_config: commercial_rate approval module (v1): same two modes as fee_waiver (intake_review | routed_task). custody.referral_to_proper_custodian.summary: If a request goes to the wrong office, that office must promptly forward it to the appropriate office; if promptly forwarded, the response clock starts when the correct office receives it.
custody.referral_to_proper_custodian.clock_spec: response time limit begins when request is received by the office specified by rule

custody.referral_to_proper_custodian.summary: If the entity does not maintain the requested record, it must, within the response window, notify the requester and provide (if known) the name and address of the entity that does maintain it.

special_records.special_production_const.summary: An entity may not provide a record it received as a shared record under § 63G-2-206; it must deny the request and inform the requester of the identity of the entity from which the shared record was received.

redaction.third_party_claim.summary: A person who provides a record they believe should be protected as a trade secret/commercial information under 63G-2-305(1)/(2) must provide, with or within a reasonable time after the record, a written claim of business confidentiality and a concise statement of supporting reasons.

Disposition.caps.label: REQUESTOR-LEDGER CHECK (class D)

intake.duplicate_request_denial.summary: A single record request may not be submitted to multiple governmental entities (though identical separate requests to each entity are allowed).
An entity is not required to fulfill a request that unreasonably duplicates prior records requests from that same person.

Disposition.caps.note: Requestor-ledger class-D delivery caps (OH) ride on ledger config; see ledger section.

acknowledgment.note: No statutory timer — city operational target only (soft-standard pattern S-002).

response.initial_decision_window.summary: A governmental entity must respond (approve/provide, deny, disclaim custody, or claim extraordinary circumstances) as soon as reasonably possible but no later than 10 business days after receiving a written request.
If the requester demonstrates that an expedited response benefits the public rather than the person, the entity must respond no later than 5 business days after receiving the request.

In its records ordinance/policy, a political subdivision may establish reasonable response times and appeal time limits different from those in § 63G-2-204 and Part 4 if it determines its resources are insufficient to meet those sections.

response.extension_grounds.summary: For voluminous/high-volume/locate-review grounds and for grounds requiring computer programming, the entity must disclose located records the requester may inspect, give an estimate of time to finish, and complete and disclose as soon as reasonably possible.

response.extension_length.clock_spec: ceiling: 5 business-days after the original response time expires

response.extension_length.summary: Where segregating disclosable from non-disclosable information requires extensive editing, the entity must fulfill the request within 15 business days from the date of the original request.
response.extension_length.clock_spec: ceiling: 15 business-days from date of original request

response.extension_notice.summary: If extraordinary circumstances prevent immediate approval or denial, the entity must, within the response window, notify the requester with a description of the circumstances and the date the records will be available.
response.extension_notice.clock_spec: undefined-soft: extension period per Subsection (7), stated as a 'date when the records will be available'

media.label: Electronic media (CD/DVD/USB) charge
media.unit: USD or actual cost per medium (city sets by ordinance/policy under the actual-cost standard)
media.notes: No statewide media charge. Electronic copies must be provided in lieu of paper when requested and the record is maintained electronically without reformatting (§ 63G-2-201(13)); a medium not currently maintained is discretionary and chargeable 'in accordance with Section 63G-2-203' (§ 63G-2-201(8…

delivery.label: Delivery: mail / handling / email / pickup
delivery.unit: USD or actual cost (city sets by ordinance/policy under the actual-cost standard)
delivery.authority: Utah Code § 63G-2-203(1)(a), (2)(a)(ii), (3)(c); Archives GRAMA Request for Payment or Prepayment (2025) line item 'Mailing or shipping cost'
delivery.notes: No statutory postage/handling figure; mailing is an actual/direct administrative cost of providing the record and the Archives official payment form carries a 'Mailing or shipping cost' line. certification.label: Certification / certified-copy charge
certification.unit: USD per certified copy (city sets 'lawful fees' by ordinance/policy under the actual-cost standard)
certification.authority: Utah Code § 63G-2-201(6); § 63G-2-203(1)(a), (3)(c), (9); Archives payment form line 'Certification fee'
certification.notes: A certified copy must be provided when the requester has a right to inspect, identifies the record with reasonable specificity, and 'pays the lawful fees' (§ 63G-2-201(6)); GRAMA sets no certification figure and § 63G-2-203(9) preserves fees fixed by other statutes (none found for municipal recor…

av.label: Audio/video: per recording, per minute, free minutes
av.unit: USD per recording / per minute (city sets by ordinance/policy under the actual-cost standard); no free-minutes rule
av.notes: No audio/video-specific fee provision in GRAMA (§ 63G-2-203 searched in full) or in the body-worn-camera chapter (Utah Code Title 77, Ch. 7a, chapter index reviewed — no fee section). commercial.label: Commercial-purpose schedule (surcharge %, labor becomes chargeable)
commercial.notes: Utah has no commercial-purpose fee regime: labor is chargeable for every requester alike (after the free quarter hour), and purpose matters only (a) as a discretionary waiver ground — release 'primarily benefits the public rather than a person' (§ 63G-2-203(4)(a)); (b) for the expedited-response …

waiver.label: Fee waiver: grounds, mandatory vs discretionary, purpose statement, written denial, appeal
waiver.value: discretionary ('may ... and is encouraged to'); grounds: (a) release primarily benefits the public rather than a person, (b) requester is the subject of the record or a § 63G-2-202(1)/(2) person, (c) requester's legal rights are directly implicated and requester is impecunious; mandatory = false; purpose statement not required by law (official form invites justification); written denial not expressly required; appeal: to chief administrative officer within 30 days of notice of denial, then GRO director / local appeals board / court, de novo review
waiver.notes: Waiver is discretionary but 'encouraged' on three statutory grounds; no requester purpose statement is required by statute (GRAMA never requires a purpose), though the Archives GRAMA Request Form invites the requester to tick waiver grounds and 'Explain other justification'. waiver.forfeiture.label: Late response forfeits the fee
waiver.forfeiture.notes: A late response is a deemed denial (§ 63G-2-204(9)) — it triggers appeal rights, not loss of the fee. No forfeiture rule in statute, rule, or Archives guidance. repeat.label: Repeat / aggregated requests (carry-forward, aggregation threshold)
repeat.value: (a) fee carry-forward: a non-Utah-media requester who submitted a separate request within the 10 days before the current request loses the free first quarter hour (10-day look-back per requestor); (b) no fee aggregation threshold; related non-fee rules: entity need not fulfill a request that 'unreasonably duplicates prior records requests from that person' (§ 63G-2-201(7)(a)(iv)); a substantial number of records requested within five working days of each other is an 'extraordinary circumstance' extending the response clock (§ 63G-2-204(6)(c)(ii)); vexatious-requester relief (§ 63G-2-209)
repeat.notes: The only fee-side repeat rule is the 10-day look-back that strips the free quarter hour from non-media repeat requesters (UT-0036). Utah has no cost-aggregation threshold across requests. The duplication, five-working-day clustering, and vexatious-requester provisions are processing/clock rules, …

fee.labor_charge.summary: An hourly staff-time charge may not exceed the salary of the lowest paid employee who has the necessary skill and training to perform the request.

fee.actual_cost_basis.summary: An entity may charge a reasonable fee to cover its actual cost of providing a record; the fee must be approved by the entity's executive officer.

When compiling a record in a form other than normally maintained, actual costs may include staff time for compiling/formatting/tailoring, staff time for search/retrieval and direct administrative costs, and (for non-word-processing computer output) actual incremental cost plus a reasonable portio…

fee.free_allowance.summary: An entity may not charge a fee for the first quarter hour of staff time spent responding to a request.

The free first quarter hour does not apply if the requester is not a Utah media representative AND previously submitted a separate request within the 10-day period immediately before the current request.

fee.no_charge_categories.summary: An entity may not charge a fee for reviewing a record to determine whether it is subject to disclosure, except as permitted for search/retrieval staff time under 203(2)(a)(ii).

fee.schedule_and_authority.summary: Political subdivisions must establish records fees by ordinance or written formal policy adopted by the governing body.

custody.records_officer_designation.summary: A governmental entity may make rules specifying where and to whom requests for access must be directed.

fee.schedule_and_authority.summary: Political subdivisions must establish records fees by ordinance or written formal policy adopted by the governing body.

intake.duplicate_request_denial.summary: A single record request may not be submitted to multiple governmental entities (though identical separate requests to each entity are allowed).
An entity is not required to fulfill a request that unreasonably duplicates prior records requests from that same person.

payment.advance_payment.summary: An entity may require payment of past fees and future estimated fees before beginning to process a request.
payment.advance_payment.clock_spec: undefined-soft: processing withheld until prepayment received ('before beginning to process a request')

payment.advance_payment.summary: Prepayment may be required when fees are expected to exceed $50.
Any prepaid amount in excess of fees due must be returned to the requester.
